title: FIFA World Cup Final to Feature First-Ever Halftime Show With Madonna, Shakira and BTS
excerpt: An 11-minute spectacle curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin will break 96 years of World Cup tradition at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, combining star power with a $100 million education fundraiser.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The first-ever FIFA World Cup Final halftime show features Madonna, Shakira, BTS, and Justin Bieber.
  • The 11-minute performance aims to raise $100 million for children's education and football access.
  • Guest performers include Burna Boy, Gustavo Dudamel, and the PS22 Chorus from Staten Island.
  • The extended halftime has faced criticism for potentially disrupting players' routines.
  • The show will be broadcast live to an estimated two billion viewers worldwide.
A Historic Halftime Show
›First halftime show in FIFA World Cup history.
›11-minute performance featuring major artists.
›Curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin.
›Scheduled during the Spain vs. Argentina final.
https://x.com/CarolRadull/status/2078458009831854253
  • Madonna, Shakira, BTS, and Justin Bieber will co-headline the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final halftime show on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
  • The 11-minute performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin and produced by Global Citizen, aims to raise $100 million for education and football access for children worldwide.
  • Guest performers include Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel, the PS22 Chorus from Staten Island, and Coldplay, with appearances by The Muppets and Sesame Street characters.
  • The extended halftime has drawn criticism from football purists who say it violates the sport's 15-minute interval rule and could disrupt players' routines.

A Historic Break From Tradition

For 96 years, the FIFA World Cup Final operated without a halftime show. On Sunday, that changes.

When Spain and Argentina walk off the pitch at MetLife Stadium during the 2026 World Cup Final, the first-ever dedicated halftime performance in World Cup history will take over the field. The 11-minute show will feature co-headliners Madonna, Shakira, BTS, and Justin Bieber, supported by guest performers Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel, the PS22 Chorus, and Coldplay.

Chris Martin, Coldplay's frontman, is curating the lineup. Global Citizen is producing it alongside Live Nation and Done+Dusted. The show is set against the backdrop of the Spain-Argentina final, with kickoff scheduled for 3 p.m. ET.

Star Power Meets Social Purpose

The performance is built around the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, a joint initiative between FIFA and Global Citizen launched in September 2024. The fund aims to raise $100 million to expand access to quality education and football programs for children in underserved communities worldwide. FIFA has pledged $1 from every ticket sold during the tournament to the fund, which has already raised more than $50 million toward its target.

None of the headliners are receiving performance fees. Sources confirmed to The Athletic that Madonna, Shakira, and BTS are donating their time to the social justice organization.

"I've spent my life doing two things — making songs and building schools. At the FIFA World Cup, those two paths come together."

- Shakira, in the official FIFA press release

Shakira's World Cup connection runs deep. She performed at the 2006 closing ceremony in Berlin, recorded the iconic 2010 anthem "Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)," and co-wrote "Dai Dai" with Burna Boy — the official 2026 tournament song that currently sits at No. 1 on both Billboard Global Charts. Madonna brings her own Super Bowl halftime experience from 2012, while BTS represents the global reach of K-pop. Justin Bieber, added to the lineup on July 8, makes one of his most prominent televised appearances since returning to regular music activity.

Beyond the Music: Muppets, Dudamel, and a Staten Island Choir

The show's guest lineup reflects Martin's eclectic curation. Gustavo Dudamel, the internationally acclaimed conductor and Music and Artistic Director of the New York Philharmonic, will perform alongside the PS22 Chorus, a Webby Award-winning elementary school choir from Staten Island, New York. Characters from The Muppets and Sesame Street will also appear — a choice FIFA says reinforces the show's education-focused mission.

Coldplay will perform as well, rounding out a bill that spans pop, Latin music, K-pop, Afrobeats, classical orchestration, and children's programming in a single 11-minute window.

The Controversy Around the Clock

The extended halftime has generated pushback from football purists. Law 7 of the Laws of the Game states that halftime intervals should not exceed 15 minutes. BBC Sport reported on July 14 that the total halftime is expected to last between 20 and 25 minutes, with the 11-minute show starting after the standard 15-minute break. The Atlantic reported FIFA was targeting no more than 20 minutes total.

Sports journalist Gabriele Marcotti captured the tension: "Professional footballers are conditioned to 15-minute breaks. They're athletes. Mess with their routine and they'll get cold, or hot, or stiff or whatever. It's not worth the risk of screwing with this."

The BBC initially planned to skip the show during its main television coverage, intending to run pundit analysis instead. ITV reportedly followed suit. But as of July 15, both UK broadcasters reversed course and confirmed they will air the halftime performance.

Pre-Game Spectacle Adds Even More Star Power

The halftime show is only part of the day's entertainment. A separate closing ceremony at 1:30 p.m. ET will feature appearances by Tom Cruise, performances from Post Malone, Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger, Italian singer Laura Pausini, and online creator IShowSpeed. Jennifer Hudson will perform the U.S. national anthem. FOX will air a four-hour pregame show starting at 11 a.m. ET, with stadium gates opening at the same time.

A Global Stage With Indian Resonance

For Indian diaspora fans, the show's appeal extends beyond the football. BTS commands a massive and devoted fanbase across India, and Shakira's music has long been woven into Bollywood remix culture and South Asian celebrations. The show will broadcast live to an estimated two billion viewers worldwide — a number FIFA President Gianni Infantino has called "definitely the biggest stage ever."

Whether the halftime show becomes a permanent fixture of future World Cup Finals remains an open question. FIFA has made no announcement either way. Sunday's reception will serve as the test case for whether football's biggest match can accommodate the kind of entertainment spectacle that the Super Bowl made a cultural institution.
